title: Runtime sentinel-driven canary and dynamic failover
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Implement a sentinel-driven canary and automated dynamic failover system that protects customer SLOs during model variant rollouts across regions and capacity tiers. This ticket designs the runtime orchestration + control-plane hooks needed to run small percentage canaries, mirror shadow traffic safely, continuously score quality/latency, and perform automated, staged failovers (region, tier, or model variant) when pre-defined sentinels breach thresholds. The approach emphasizes safe, reversible actions and observability for on-call response.

Background: Current rollout primitives allow traffic splitting and simple rollbacks but lack a continuous automated safety net that considers downstream quality regressions, KV cache warmup, and tiered capacity constraints. We need a runtime component ("Sentinel Engine") that watches streaming metrics, computes per-variant risk scores, and orchestrates traffic shifts (ramp-up, throttle, or rollback) across regions and capacity tiers.

Goals:
- Provide an automated canary guard that can stop or rollback rollouts based on latency, error-rate, and quality regressions detected by prompt-set evals.
- Support shadowing/mirroring with isolated metrics and storage to avoid polluting production logs and billing.
- Enable tier-aware admission and cross-region failover with graceful KV cache handoff and warmup hints.
- Keep all actions reversible and auditable with runbook links and automatic rollback reason codes.

Design highlights:
- Sentinel Engine: a lightweight control-plane service that subscribes to the metrics stream (latency P50/P95/P99, token-rate, 5xx rate, per-prompt quality signals). It exposes a policy evaluator that consumes rules (thresholds, hysteresis, cooldown) and a scoring function producing a real-time risk score for each (region, model-variant, tier) tuple.
- Actions supported: pause ramp, step-down percentage, redirect traffic to fallback variant, regional drain + redirect, preemptive admission control (reject or queue), automatic rollback with snapshot tag.
- Compatibility handshake: before routing traffic to a variant, runtime performs a lightweight compatibility check (tokenizer/version handshake, KV-cache size estimates, expected max-seqlen). If handshake fails, variant is placed into 'incompatible' pool and only receives shadow traffic for debugging.
- KV cache warmup: when promoting a canary to higher %, the runtime emits 'warmup hints' to dedicated workers to prefetch prefixes for hot prompts (based on recent requests) to reduce cold-start latency. Warmup progress is exposed to Sentinel to avoid fast ramps if warmup incomplete.
- Tier-aware policies: policies can be scoped per-capacity-tier (e.g., dedicated-gpu, burst, hosted-lowcost). For lower tiers, Sentinel enforces stricter SLO margins and more conservative ramp increments.
- Shadow traffic isolation: mirrored requests are marked and routed to instrumented instances with suppressed billing and separate telemetry sink. Quality metrics from shadows are correlated but do not affect production quotas unless explicitly promoted.

API and configuration:
- New rollout API endpoints: POST /rollouts/{id}/sentinel-config to attach policies; GET /rollouts/{id}/sentinel-status for live risk score and action history.
- Policy schema (YAML/JSON): thresholds, primary metrics, cooldown, rollback actions, allowed fallback variants, cross-region failover order, tier-priority list.

Metrics and rollback triggers:
- Latency: P95 > baseline * 1.25 for 5m AND P99 > baseline * 1.5 => risk += high
- Errors: 5xx rate > 0.5% for 3m => immediate pause and investigate
- Quality: Average prompt-set score delta <= -3% for sliding window of 200 samples => initiate canary step-down or rollback depending on severity
- Cache: cold-start rate increase > 30% compared to baseline => slow ramp and prefetch; if persists, rollback to variant that shares cache layout

Success criteria:
- Sentinel halts bad rollouts automatically at least 90% of the time on synthetic regressions injected in staging and 95% in canary trials.
- Mean time to mitigate (auto actions) < 3 minutes from sentinel breach for high-severity rules.
- No customer-visible errors introduced by shadow traffic in production (verified for 30-day window).
- Rollout API surfaces actionable reason codes and a reversible rollback snapshot.

Operational runbook (short):
- On sentinel pause: open the Sentinel dashboard, review last 10k requests for divergence, check warmup progress, and decide to resume or rollback.
- On auto-rollback: verify rollback snapshot status and announce via #deployments channel with reason code.

Out of scope for this ticket: integrating full ML-based quality detectors (we use prompt-set heuristics and simple embedding drift for now), and policy UI in Console (Console will read status via API in a follow-up ticket).
acceptance_criteria: Sentinel Engine deployed to staging and able to subscribe to runtime metrics stream
Policy evaluator accepts JSON policy and returns risk score for sample rollout
Runtime applies pause/step-down/redirect actions based on policy in staging canary runs
Shadow traffic sinked to isolated telemetry and does not affect billing or quotas
Compatibility handshake rejects an intentionally-incompatible variant and flags it in status
Automated rollback emits a snapshot tag and an audit event with reason code
rollout_plan: Week 1: Implement Sentinel Engine skeleton and policy schema; unit tests for evaluator
Week 2: Wire to metrics stream and add action executor for pause/step-down/redirect in staging
Week 3: Integrate tokenizer/kv-cache compatibility handshake and warmup hints
Week 4: End-to-end staging canary tests with synthetic regressions and shadow traffic runs
Week 5: Gradual production rollout behind feature flag; limit to internal customers then expand
monitoring_and_alerting: Primary metric: per-rollout risk_score (0-100) streamed to console and alerts when > 70
Alert: Auto-rollback executed -> page on-call and post incident stub to #deployments
SLO guard: if P95 latency increases > 20% for 10 minutes across >1% of users -> emergency traffic diversion
Dashboard: rollout timeline with actions, warmup progress, and per-prompt quality deltas
testing_plan: Unit tests for policy evaluator and action executor (simulate metrics)
Integration test: staging canary that intentionally regresses quality to validate auto-pause and rollback
Chaos test: simulate regional outage and verify cross-region failover ordering and TTL-preserving retry
Performance test: ensure Sentinels add <5% overhead to control-plane latency under 5k concurrent rollouts
